issues.evidence: static/A-ruff.txt (25 findings in task_manager.py: UP031 %-format, E501, B904, B905)
issues.summary: Style lint findings: old-style %-formatting, long lines, raise without 'from'.
UPDATE SET clause built by string formatting; keys come from fixed kwargs so not exploitable, values are parameterized.
Filter values are validated in code rather than with argparse choices, so --help does not list the allowed values.
Whitespace-only/empty titles are accepted and stored.

issues.evidence: probe P21_bad_db_path: Traceback ... sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file
issues.summary: sqlite3 errors are not caught, so the user sees a raw traceback.
list truncates titles over 30 chars and descriptions over 40 chars with an ellipsis; full text is only visible via the extra 'show' command.

issues.evidence: B: `update 1 --due none` -> 'Nothing to update.' rc=1 (valid_date maps 'none' to None, which is then filtered out); B/task_manager.py:35,103
issues.summary: valid_date accepts 'none' but update ignores it, which is confusing; --clear-due is the working path.
Default database is ~/.tasks.db in the home directory (overridable with --db/TASK_DB).

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt (8 findings: E731 lambda, B904, B905, E501, S608)

blinding_guess.why: Both are compact single-file argparse CLIs with near-identical schemas; A's separated domain functions plus tests hint at a more disciplined process, but that is weak evidence.

notes: Both sides use the same CLI shape (add/list/update/done/delete with -p/-s/--due/--db), so every probe used the same invocation with --db pointed at a temp file. A passed all 23 probes and its 7 unittest tests pass. B passed 20 of 23: it accepts empty titles, shows a traceback when the database path cannot be opened, and truncates long fields in the table. B adds extras (show command, --clear-due, priority/due-date sorting) but has no tests. Both build the UPDATE SET clause dynamically from fixed column names with parameterized values; bandit B608 is a false positive on both.
